reasoning: By Mantel's theorem (the r=2 case of Turán's theorem), a triangle-free simple graph on n vertices has at most floor(n^2/4) edges. For n=13 this is floor(169/4)=42. Proof sketch: for any edge uv in a triangle-free graph, N(u) and N(v) are disjoint, so deg(u)+deg(v) <= n; summing over edges gives sum of deg(v)^2 <= n*m, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives (2m)^2/n <= sum deg^2 <= n*m, so m <= n^2/4. Construction achieving 42: the complete bipartite graph K_{6,7} — split the 13 vertices into parts A (6 vertices) and B (7 vertices) and join every vertex of A to every vertex of B. It has 6*7=42 edges and is bipartite, hence contains no odd cycle and in particular no triangle.
